newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm, poised to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm, poised to strengthen.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was marginally firm against the dollar on Tuesday and poised to strengthen further on coffee and tea inflows expected later in the day, commercial bank dealers said.

The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean average of 52.96 against the dollar, compared with 53.05 on Monday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at a commercial mean of 86.50 from 86.88.

With low levels of demand seen as insignificant to move the market, dealers said the shilling would strengthen, especially if the central bank stayed out of the market as a buyer of last resort to allow the shilling to find its own equilibrium level.
Senior economists who closely monitor the central bank said the bank believed the shilling was still very undervalued.
"The shilling is rangebound trading at 52.80/53.10. The 53 level is the next test for the shilling as dollars from export sales come in later, today," one dealer said.
The money market tightened on tax outflows. Overnight rates were quoted at 20 percent levels from 15 percent on Monday.
